title: Finite orthogonality classes in locally finitely presentable categories
statement: Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C$ be an ordinary category formed in $\mathcal V$ with $\mathcal U$-small Hom sets. Assume that $\mathcal C$ is locally finitely presentable relative to $\mathcal U$: it has all $\mathcal U$-small colimits and a $\mathcal U$-small family of finitely presentable objects generating every object under $\mathcal U$-small filtered colimits. An object $P$ is finitely presentable if $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(P,-)$ preserves these filtered colimits, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $S$ be a $\mathcal U$-small set of morphisms $s:P_s\to Q_s$ whose domains and codomains are finitely presentable. Write $S^\perp$ for the full subcategory on the objects $X$ for which precomposition $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(Q_s,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(P_s,X)$ is a bijection for every $s\in S$. Then $S^\perp$ is locally finitely presentable relative to $\mathcal U$, with the same colimit-and-filtered-generator meaning as above.
